title: Linzer Tart
identity: Linzer Tart is one of six selections in Claude Delvincourt’s Croquembouches, arranged for alto saxophone and piano by Jean-Marie Londeix. Wind Music’s library catalog gives a total duration of 12:25 for the collection. A separate Spotify listing identifies a 1:56 track with Christopher Creviston and Hannah Gruber, but the recording’s version/instrument is not established. Scott D. Kallestad’s 2005 UNT dissertation includes Croquembouches in its survey of college saxophone faculty repertoire lists; one list labeled it sophomore, which is historical evidence rather than a current level recommendation.

evidence.claim: Library catalog identifies the six-piece Croquembouches collection, including Linzer Tart, for alto saxophone and piano, arranged by Jean-Marie Londeix; duration is 12:25 for the whole collection.
Montpellier Médiathèques provides an institutional catalog record for the six-piece alto-saxophone/piano collection and includes Linzer Tart in contents.
Spotify metadata lists “Croquembouches: Linzer tart” at 1:56 with Christopher Creviston and Hannah Gruber; exact edition/instrument was not verified.
The guide’s entry lists Linzer Tart as movement 4 with an estimated duration of 1:30; 12:25 is the full set duration.
evidence.source_name: Claude Delangle et al., 10 ans avec le saxophone (Philharmonie de Paris digital scan)

evidence.claim: In a 2005 DMA study based on selected college and university saxophone repertoire lists, Croquembouches appears on one list and is labeled sophomore by that list. The dissertation explicitly reports the label and count as survey results.
evidence.source_name: Scott D. Kallestad, University of North Texas DMA dissertation (2005)

review_focus: Inference from the 1993 guide’s movement description: review the contrast between the waltz pulse and its allegro non troppo character, and assess the set within its short miniature format. No saxophone notation was inspected.
collection_flag: An arrangement of a piano miniature within a six-piece Londeix saxophone/piano set. The college-list study demonstrates historical college programming use; its single-list sophomore label is not a current or recommended SaxoBrain level.
